[id=S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1]
Stability of Global Minima.
[id=S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1] We state that every global minimum is Lyapunov stable under SpecGF with 𝒯β\mathcal{T}_{\beta}. Lyapunov stability is standard for describing whether trajectories that start near an equilibrium remain near it over time.
Definition 6.6 (Lyapunov stability).
[id=S6.Thmtheorem6.p1.1] A critical point 𝐱¯∈𝐑d\bar{\mathbf{x}}\in\mathbf{R}^{d} is Lyapunov stable if for every neighborhood Uϵ⊂𝐑dU_{\epsilon}\subset\mathbf{R}^{d} of 𝐱¯\bar{\mathbf{x}}, there exists a neighborhood Uδ⊂𝐑dU_{\delta}\subset\mathbf{R}^{d} of 𝐱¯\bar{\mathbf{x}} such that for all 𝐱⁡(t)\mathbf{x}(t) with 𝐱⁡(0)∈Uδ\mathbf{x}(0)\in U_{\delta}, 𝐱⁡(t)∈Uϵ\mathbf{x}(t)\in U_{\epsilon} for all t≥0t\geq 0.
[id=S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1] If then, any starting point near some global minima cannot go far away from that global minimum. By Proposition 6.4, bounded SpecGF iterations should converge to a critical point. The stability of the global minima is proved by Lemma 6.5; see Theorem D.15 for details. Therefore, the local convergence of SpecGF with 𝒯β\mathcal{T}_{\beta} is always guaranteed.
[id=S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2]
Convergence Rate.
[id=S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1] The convergence rate of SpecGF with 𝒯β\mathcal{T}_{\beta} readily follows by Lemma 6.5. Assume that SpecGF converges to a global minimum. We show that the loss function is essentially Morse-Bott, whose optimal exponent in the Łojasiewicz inequality is 12\frac{1}{2}, leading to exponential convergence;
see Section D.5 for detailed proof.
Proposition 6.7 (Informal).
[id=S6.Thmtheorem7.p1.1] Assume that the singular values of 𝐘\mathbf{Y} are mutually distinct. If SpecGF with 𝒯β\mathcal{T}_{\beta} converges to a global minimum of ℒ\mathcal{L}, then it exponentially converges in terms of ℒ⁡(t)\mathcal{L}(t).
[id=S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1] The assumption of distinct singular values of the target matrix is also considered in previous studies (Gidel et al., 2019; Jin et al., 2023).
Remark 6.8.
[id=S6.Thmtheorem8.p1.1] Assume that both ∇𝐀ℒ​(t)\nabla_{\mathbf{A}}\mathcal{L}(t) and ∇𝐁ℒ​(t)\nabla_{\mathbf{B}}\mathcal{L}(t) are full-rank throughout SpecGF with 𝒯\mathcal{T}. Then SpecGF with 𝒯\mathcal{T} is analytic, and the same arguments for SpecGF with 𝒯β\mathcal{T}_{\beta} hold. Moreover, if SpecGF with 𝒯\mathcal{T} converges, then it should converge in finite time; see Proposition D.18 for details.
[id=S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3]
Global Convergence via Regularization.
[id=S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1] Adding a ℓ2\ell_{2} regularizer guarantees global convergence of SpecGF with 𝒯β\mathcal{T}_{\beta}.
All theoretical claims for SpecGF with 𝒯β\mathcal{T}_{\beta} also apply to the regularized SpecGF with 𝒯β\mathcal{T}_{\beta}. Moreover, boundedness of 𝐀\mathbf{A} and 𝐁\mathbf{B} readily follows from the regularization; see Section D.6 for details. Therefore, regularized SpecGF with 𝒯β\mathcal{T}_{\beta} globally converges to the global minima almost surely.

7 Empirical Validation of Our Theory
[id=S7.p1.1] In this section, we validate our theoretical results. In particular, we confirm the uniform growth of singular values under SpecGF and the equal-rate learning behavior.

[id=S8]
8 Conclusion
[id=S8.p1.1] We analyzed spectral gradient flow (SpecGF) for LoRA-style matrix factorization and proved that singular values of the product 𝐀𝐁\mathbf{A}\mathbf{B} exhibit uniform growth, leading to a “equal-rate” learning that contrasts with the largest-first behavior of standard gradient flow. We also established that SpecGF almost surely converges to global minima; with ℓ2\ell_{2} regularization, global convergence is also guaranteed. We validated our theory via experiments on matrix factorization and LLM fine-tuning. A key limitation is that global convergence without regularization remains open due to the absence of known invariants for SpecGF. Extending our continuous-time analysis to discrete-time SpecGD and more general network architectures is an important future work.
[id=Sx1]
Impact Statement
[id=Sx1.p1.1] This paper presents work whose goal is to advance the field of machine learning. There are many potential societal consequences of our work, none of which we feel must be specifically highlighted here.
